questions.q: Why does Howard Okonjo make the ask while Mara Voss stays ready to defend specific numbers?
options: Mara is not allowed to speak in board meetings
Howard frames the headline and the decision for a body evaluating risk, while Mara, as the engineer who built the pilot and automation, can credibly defend any number the board pushes on
Howard built the automation himself, so only he understands the details
The board only ever asks questions of the CISO, never the engineer
questions.explain: Splitting the roles this way gives the board a clear non-technical headline from Howard and a credible technical answer from Mara if anyone digs into the specifics.

questions.q: How is the audit/SIEM discrepancy disclosed to the board, according to this lesson?
options: It's left off the slides entirely since it's already fixed
It's disclosed plainly: two independent methods disagreed, the root cause was found and fixed, and both now agree — framed as evidence the program is working
It's described only as 'a minor technical issue' with no further detail
It's presented as proof the audit team made a serious error
questions.explain: The honest version is also the stronger version — it demonstrates the two-independent-checks design catching a real gap exactly as intended.

questions.q: What is 'the ask' in this board presentation, and why does it matter?
options: There is no ask; this meeting is purely informational

Approve funding and headcount to extend zero-trust segmentation and the corrected audit methodology to the next OT segment — without it, the report is just a status update with nothing for the board to decide
Ask the board to personally review the Python automation's source code
Ask the board to replace Renee Castellano as Compliance Officer
questions.explain: A board report with no decision attached wastes the board's actual purpose; the ask gives them something concrete to approve, backed by the results already shown.

questions.q: What does the zero-trust pilot's reported result show about standing OT/SCADA admin access?
options: It grew from 12 to 17 accounts with no explanation
It was cut from 17 untracked accounts to 13 governed ones, with the remaining break-glass pattern now time-boxed and logged
All admin access was eliminated entirely
It remains exactly as it was before the pilot began
questions.explain: The pilot's real result is a reduction to a fully governed, time-boxed set of accounts — not zero admin access, but zero untracked admin access.

questions.q: Why would hiding the discrepancy have been the wrong choice for this board presentation?
options: Because board members would have found out anyway from a news report
Because it would have hidden the clearest evidence that the zero-trust program's two-independent-checks design is actually paying off
Because hiding findings from a board is illegal in all cases
Because the discrepancy was never actually resolved
questions.explain: The discrepancy being caught and fixed is itself the strongest proof of the program's value — hiding it would mean hiding that proof.
